newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-SUPER LEAGUE PULLS OUT OF PEACE TALKS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-SUPER LEAGUE PULLS OUT OF PEACE TALKS.

text.p: A bid to resolve Australian rugby league's protracted and bitter feud stalled on Monday when Rupert Murdoch's Super League walked out of talks with a rival ruling body over a unified competition next year.
Super League executive director Ian Frykberg blamed the Australian Rugby League (ARL) for the setback, describing its terms for a merger as "unrealistic and unreasonable".
Frykberg said the contentious issues related to financial and administrative control of the single competition.
Despite halting negotiations, Frykberg said he was still hopeful an agreement could be reached with the ARL in time to allow for a unified league next season.
Super League, funded by Murdoch's News Ltd, the Australian arm of his global media empire, launched Super League in March. Matches are screened on Murdoch's pay television channels.
It was founded in direct competition with the ARL premiership, which is backed financially by rival pay television operator, Optus Communications.
Since the split, crowds and television ratings have plummeted as the two sides waged a bitter fight for domination in the sport's strongest playing nation.

"Super League remains committed to unity and has made significant concessions in good faith, but it is pointless for us to remain negotiating with the ARL while Optus drives another agenda," Frykberg.
ARL chief executive Neil Whittaker told a news conference that Super League's actions raised questions as to the strength of its commitment to finding a settlement.
"It is difficult to believe an organisation committed to the process would walk away before even discussing the issues we raised," Whittaker said.
